newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish government makes economic pact with left.
newsitem.headline: Danish government makes economic pact with left.

text.p: Denmark's centre-left minority government on Monday said that it had agreed with far-left parliamentary parties on a package of economic measures designed to protect the environment and swell state coffers.

Analysts said that the measures, expected to increase state revenue by about two billion crowns annually, constituted an additional fiscal tightening, designed to pre-empt any overheating in the Danish economy.
A government statement presented the package -- including new vehicle, road and fuel taxes, a passenger tax on domestic air travel and lower public transport fares -- as a green initiative.
Finance ministry officials said that they expected details of the package's likely fiscal effect to become available later in the day.

The package is subject to ratification in parliament but should be assured a safe passage. The two leftist parties, the Socialist People's Party and the Unity List command 19 seats in the 179-member assembly which, added to the 76 votes of the government and its allies, give the bill a clear majority.

The agreement cuts bus and train fares by 10 percent and raises the upper limit for child fares to 15 years from 12. It raises the rate of road tax for commercial vehicles also used for private journeys and alters duty on new cars to encourage the purchase of smaller, less polluting models.
Vehicles meeting latest EU environmental criteria will pay a reduced rate of road tax and petrol would be taxed according to the amount of benzene it contained.
Benzene is a constituent of petrol, which the statement said can cause leukaemia.

Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft told reporters that the deal did not oblige the Socialist People's Party and the Unity List to support his 1998 budget, due to be unveiled in draft form in August for passage by the end of the year.
